#### Dr. Amish Shah, D-Arizona's 1st Congressional District
Dr. Amish Shah, MD, MPH is an Indian-American physician who was a member of the Arizona House of Representatives from 2019-2024. In his five years at the State Legislature, Dr. Shah had more bills signed into law than any Arizona Democrat in the last decade. He is now running for United States Congress in Arizona’s First Congressional District, one of the top pick-up opportunities for Democrats in the entire country. Dr. Shah is known throughout Arizona for his grassroots campaign efforts. Over the last seven years, he has personally knocked on nearly 20,000 doors to meet his constituents face-to-face. Many of his bills originated from a conversation at a door with a constituent. In addition to awards for his legislative activities, Dr. Shah has garnered acclaim for both his community and medical service. Dr. Shah still enjoys seeing patients and practicing Emergency Medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Phoenix, and is a practicing follower of Jainism.
Learn More

#### Rep. Dr. Rich McCormick, R-Georgia's 7th Congressional District
Dr. Rich McCormick is an Emergency Physician and is serving his second term in the US House. Rich has stood with the community on Hinduphobia and Pakistan supported terrorism against Indians in Kashmir and the Kashmiri Hindu exodus. He has strong connections with the local Hindu and Indian American community. Rich is a graduate of Morehouse School of Medicine where he was also student body president, and completed residency in Emergency Medicine through Emory while training at Grady Hospital in Atlanta. He also received his MBA from National University in California. With over 20 years in the U.S. Marine Corps and Navy, Rich served in combat zones in Africa, the Persian Gulf, and Afghanistan. As a Marine, he flew helicopters and taught at Georgia Tech and Morehouse College as the Marine Officer Instructor. In the Navy, Rich earned the rank of Commander and served as the Department Head for the Emergency Medicine Department in Kandahar, Afghanistan.

#### Rep. Shri Thanedar, D-Michigan's 13th Congressional District
Shri Thanedar, an immigrant, scientist, entrepreneur, and father, epitomizes the American dream through his journey from humble beginnings in India to a successful entrepreneur creating over 500 jobs. With an unwavering commitment to the Hindu community, Shri founded the Hindu Caucus to combat Hinduphobia in the US, advocating for concrete steps against attacks and misinformation. He tirelessly works to prevent anti-Hindu legislation in DC, aiming to educate and raise awareness. Additionally, Shri strongly supports the US-India relationship, engaging in discussions with PM Modi to strengthen ties in medicine, energy, and supply chains. Simultaneously, he advocates for increased opportunities for immigrants, pushing for H-1B visa expansion and streamlined green card processes to boost the economy and enrich America's cultural tapestry. Shri believes that collectively, we can pave the way for a brighter, more inclusive America. He is serving his second term in the US House.
Learn More

#### Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Virginia's 10th Congressional District
Suhas Subramanyam is serving his first term in the US House representing Virginia’s 10th Congressional District. He previously served in the Virginia House and Senate. Suhas is a small business owner and former Policy Advisor to President Obama, and was the first Indian-American, South Asian, and Hindu to ever be elected into the Virginia General Assembly, and he’s the first and only Virginia legislator to ever take his oath on the Bhagavad Gita. Suhas successfully passed historic legislation to bring down drug costs, prevent toll increases, address safety and gun violence in a meaningful way, and proclaimed the month of October as Hindu Heritage Month in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

card.profile:
#### Melissa Hernandez, D-California's 14th Congressional District
Melissa Hernandez is the daughter of migrant farm workers who earned her degree in Political Science and Public Affairs from California State University, East Bay, while working and raising two children. She served two terms as Mayor of Dublin, the first Latina elected to that office, where she championed housing at all income levels, brought technology and biotech jobs to the city, and expanded access to mental health care. She was also the first Latina elected to the BART Board of Directors, where she now serves as President, and she works as Director of Healthcare Services for Alameda County Supervisor David Haubert. Melissa has stood with the Hindu American community against anti-Hindu hate, and she believes no one should have to disavow their faith to participate in public life. Her opponent, State Senator Aisha Wahab, authored SB 403, the 2023 bill that singled out the Hindu community by implying caste discrimination is inherent to Hindu Americans and subjecting them to profiling and unequal treatment under the law. The Hindu American Foundation and community groups nationwide opposed it, and Governor Newsom vetoed it. In Congress, Melissa will continue to oppose any litmus test that judges Americans by who they are rather than what they have done.
Learn More

Dr. Darshana Patel is a research scientist, working mom, and school board trustee dedicated to improving the lives of people in our community. She is now running for California Assembly District 76 because she wants to ensure that every person has the opportunity and resources to thrive. Over the past 13 years, Dr. Patel has served on local civic boards, as an elected official, a state Delegate, and as a State Commissioner. These diverse roles have allowed her to better understand the needs of both the Hindu and broader community and learn how state policies directly impact local governments, services they provide, and people they serve. card.profile:
#### State Rep. Jon Rosenthal, D-Texas Railroad Commission
Normally, the Hindu American PAC would not be endorising in the election for the Texas Railroad Commission. The three member commission regulates the production of oil and natural gas in the state of Texas, and has nothing to do with the issues affecting the Hindu American community. However, the Republican nominee for this year’s election, Bo French, has revealed himself to be an outright racist, with an now infamous tweet insinutating that Indian American students celebrating at a University of Texas football game are what’s wrong with the university. He has called for the deportation of our community and other immigrant communities regardless of legal status, calling even US citizens “foreigners”, and has made statements that show a clear preference for white Christian nationalism. Hindu American PAC believes that type of politics cannot be normalized. It is thus endorsing the Democratic nominee, State Representative Jon Rosenthal, for the Texas Railroad Commission. Rep. Rosenthal is an oil and natural gas engineer by profession and is fully qualified for the position.
Note: Due to the nature of this endorsement and the position, Rep. Rosenthal has not been asked to fill out our endorsement questionnaire.
Learn more

#### Pooja Sethi, D-Texas' 47th State House District
Pooja Sethi is a mom and public servant who served as Chair of the Travis County Democratic Party and as Chief of Staff for Texas House District 47 from 2021 to 2025. A Hindu American and the daughter of immigrants, she has consistently worked to ensure public institutions respect families of all faiths and backgrounds. In her leadership roles, Pooja publicly opposed efforts to insert the Ten Commandments and Bible teachings into public school curricula, including speaking about why public schools must not promote one religion over others. She has built a record of defending religious freedom, equal treatment under the law, and inclusive education that reflects the diversity of Texas communities. As anti-Indian racism and Hinduphobia rise across Texas and the country, Pooja continues to speak out against hate and extremism in all forms.

#### Sandeep Srivastava, D-Texas' 66th State House District
Sandeep Srivastava is a longtime Plano/Frisco resident, small business owner, and dedicated community advocate. He immigrated from India to Texas in pursuit of a better life for his family and has since built a career rooted in service and opportunity. As a business owner, Sandeep has helped build and operate childcare centers across the Dallas-Fort Worth area, working to meet the growing need for affordable, accessible childcare for working families. Sandeep is also a longtime community leader and the founder of a nonprofit organization that supports new immigrants as they transition to life in the United States, helping families build stability and succeed in their new home. He is a strong voice against Hinduphobia, xenophobia, and discrimination in all its forms, and is committed to building a community where every person feels respected. Sandeep is focused on building a broad, bipartisan coalition centered on practical solutions and real results.

#### Dr. Yang Shao, Fremont City Council
Dr. Yang Shao received a perfect score from Hindu American PAC's candidate questionnaire. He is currently serving as Councilmember in the City of Fremont, CA. From 2014-2018 he was a School Board Trustee to the Fremont Unified School District. In 2018, he served as President of the FUSD School Board and member of the Liaison Committee between FUSD School Board and Fremont City Council. He was the Vice Mayor of the City of Fremont in 2021. Currently, he also serves as Vice Chair, Housing Commission, Housing Authority of the County of Alameda. He is a board member of Citizens for Better Community and Asian Pacific Islander American Public Affairs (East Bay Chapter and Greater Fremont Chapter). He earned a Bachelor of Science degree in polymer chemistry from the University of Science and Technology of China. He earned both a Master of Arts and a Ph.D. in chemistry from Harvard University. He has been serving in the local biotechnology and biopharmaceutical industries for over 20 years.

card.profile:
#### Jag Narendra, Folsom City Council District 3
Jag Nagendra is a candidate for Folsom City Council, running to bring experienced, ethical, and community-centered leadership to one of California’s fastest-growing cities. He believes public service is about listening, building consensus, and making decisions that strengthen communities for future generations. Jag hopes to inspire greater civic participation and encourage more members of the Hindu American community to become engaged in public service. His vision is to ensure Folsom remains fiscally responsible, economically vibrant, safe, and welcoming while preserving the exceptional quality of life that residents value. With more than 35 years of professional leadership experience and over 15 years of community service, Jag has built a career centered on innovation, leadership, and service. Today, he serves as a senior technology leader with the California Department of Water Resources, leading a team of more than 60 engineers and technology professionals responsible for supporting California’s critical water infrastructure. Alongside his professional career, Jag has served on city and county boards and held leadership roles in numerous nonprofit organizations, including President of the PMI Sacramento Valley Chapter, President of the Kannada Sangha of Sacramento, President of the India Association of Davis, and Chair of the Cal Expo Cultural Advisory Council. Jag and his wife, Shyla, have proudly called Folsom home for many years. Together, they remain deeply committed to serving their community and living the values of seva, family, integrity, compassion, and responsible leadership. Jag believes that leadership is a privilege to serve others, and he is dedicated to building a stronger, more united Folsom where every resident has the opportunity to thrive.
